newsitem.title: UK: UK jobs minister says rate rise was necessary.
newsitem.headline: UK jobs minister says rate rise was necessary.

text.p: Britain's employment minister Andrew Smith said last week's interest rate increase had been necessary despite today's evidence that average earnings growth had moderated.
Asked in an interview with Reuters Financial Television if he believed average earnings growth was slowing, he replied:

"The figure has moderated and I believe that will be a welcome indicator, not only for the City, but for the economy more generally. But what really counts, of course, is the right long-term stable macro-economic framework."
Average earnings grew by an underlying 4.5 percent in the year to March and the February figure was revised down to 4.5 percent from the initial 5.0 percent.
Asked about last week's increase in official interest rates to 6.25 percent from 6.0 percent, Smith said: "The increase was necessary."

Future decisions on monetary policy would be a matter for the Bank of England but the new Labour government was putting in place a combination of measures to improve the supply side of the economy, encourage investment and raise skills, he added.
